subject: DPA / Privacy Addendum clarifications  Acme Payments
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Samantha  thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we agreed on around data handling and privacy: 

- Controller/Processor: You asked us to clarify roles. Redwood acts as a processor for customer-provided data where the customer (Acme Payments) is the controller for end-customer PII. For any telemetry we generate for product operations (aggregated metrics), Redwood is a controller for those internal analytics.

- Subprocessors: We maintain a list of subprocessors; we flagged the use of cloud infra and a managed logging provider in the call. I attached our current subprocessors list (CSV) for your review. We can notify you per the contract where there are material changes.

- Breach notice: Our standard is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that affects customer data, and to provide a full incident report as available. You asked about statutory requirements  we will align the notification timeline to any contractually required windows if specified in the Addendum.

- Data retention & logging: Default request logs (access and audit events) are retained 90 days. For model request payloads (which may contain PII), retention is configurable per account; default retention is 30 days, and we offer options to shorten or disable retention for regulated customers.

- Data residency: We support regional data residency (US, EU) for data at rest and processing. For EU residency we can commit to routing and encryption keys in-region; for strict air-gapped or on-prem needs we can discuss Private deployment options.

Next steps we discussed: 
1) I'll send the annotated DPA with inline clarifications and our subprocessors CSV (attached).
2) Ben will follow up with pricing for Dedicated/Private options if you need residency and longer retention controls.
3) If you have legal redlines, please share them and we'll circulate to our legal/security teams.

Do you want to set a 30-minute follow-up (legal + security) next week to go through the DPA? I'm free Tue/Wed afternoon PST.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_annotated_v1.pdf

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@acmepayments.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmepayments.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Thanks Marissa  helpful summary. A couple of clarifying Qs from our side before we loop legal: 

1) On controller/processor: can you confirm the definition in your DPA maps to the EU standard (i.e., we remain the controller and Redwood the processor; Redwood will only process on our documented instructions)? We need explicit language for PCI-adjacent PII.

2) Regarding subprocessors: does Redwood provide a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors, or only notification after onboarding? Our procurement prefers prior notice window to evaluate replacements.

3) For breach notice: does the 72-hour timeline start from discovery or from confirmation that customer data was affected? Some regulators expect from discovery. Clarify your commitments here.

If you can answer those 3 items and confirm whether the data retention settings can be locked by our admin (i.e., we can enforce a 0/30/90 day retention policy at the account level), we can get Acme Legal involved and send any redlines.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Security & Privacy
Acme Payments

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmepayments.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Samantha  great questions. Looping Dev (SE) and Rishi (Security) to provide the technical and contractual clarifications below. See inline answers and attached subprocessors export.

1) Controller/Processor: Yes  our DPA language mirrors the EU standard: you (Acme Payments) are the controller, Redwood is the processor and we only process on documented customer instructions. We will add explicit PCI-adjacent note in the DPA: Redwood will not use payment card data for any profiling or model training and will follow your documented instructions for handling such fields. (Rishi: please confirm operational controls below.)

2) Subprocessors notice: Our standard is to provide notice of new subprocessors by email and publish to the subprocessor registry; for most non-material cloud infra changes we currently notify after onboarding, but we can add a 30-day prior notice commitment for approved subprocessors as a contract option. We are OK putting that in the Addendum as a checkboxed option if you require it.

3) Breach notice window: Our legal stance is to notify customers within 72 hours of confirming that customer data was impacted. For regulatory alignment we can commit to notify within 72 hours of discovery for certain jurisdictions if that is contractually required. We can add clarifying language to the DPA that says: "Redwood will notify Controller without undue delay and, in any event, within 72 hours of discovery where feasible, and will follow up with remediation details as available."

4) Retention & admin controls: Yes  retention settings are configurable at the account/admin level. We can lock retention settings via an admin policy and document that in the Addendum (choices: 0/30/90 days or custom). For customers on Redwood Private we can also offer no-retention or on-prem storage options.

Operational notes from Rishi: 
- Access logs: stored for 90 days by default; can be extended on request.
- Request payloads containing PII: default 30-day retention, can be shortened to 0 days for redacted-only flow or disabled for Private deployments.
- Encryption & keys: data at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMIP/KMS) is available for Private or Dedicated customers; hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys with regional key options.

Next actions: 
- Marissa: share updated DPA with the 30-day prior-notice option and the breach language above (attached).
- Samantha / Acme Legal: review and send any redlines; if acceptable, we can prepare a DocuSign envelope.
- Ben: please include pricing for Dedicated residency + retention controls and note any lead times.

Thanks  happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk legal/security through the specific clauses.

Marissa
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmepayments.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA clarifications  next steps

Appreciate the quick follow-up and the detailed answers. Acme Legal will review the annotated DPA and the subprocessors list this week. We appreciate the offer to include the 30-day prior notice as an option  that should satisfy procurement.

We'll aim to return redlines by next Wed (Aug 4). If we need a walkthrough, I'll ping for a meeting in your shared Calendars.

Thanks,
Samantha

Acme Payments
